newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Hutchison Whampoa in Brazil cellular group.
newsitem.headline: Hutchison Whampoa in Brazil cellular group.

text.p: Hutchison Telecommunications, a unit of Hong Kong-based Hutchison Whampoa Ltd, and two Brazilian partners will jointly bid for upcoming concessions to run cellular telephone operations in Brazil, the companies said.
Hutchison Telecommunications has joined forces with Teldin, a newly created unit of electronics manufacturer Grupo Evadin, and investment bank Banco Garantia, the companies said in a statement.
The creation of the new group comes one day after the Brazilian government published rules for the upcoming bidding to run so-called B Band cellular telephone concessions.
The statement said Hutchison Telecommunications serves 2.3 million clients in ten countries across Asia and in Australia, India and Britain where it runs the Orange cellular network.

Teldin was created earlier this year by Grupo Evadin to take advantage of openings in the Brazilian telecommunications sector and the expected privatization of state holding Telebras, the statement said.
Banco Garantia administers around $600 million in private equity which it invests in Brazilian business opportunities, like the upcoming B Band operations.
The ten regional B Band concessions will be the first big step in the privatization of the country's telecommunications industry.
The number of cellular customers in Brazil is expected to grow by as much as ten times to 15 million by the year 2000, according to government estimates.

Winners of the B Band concessions will compete against regional subsidiaries of state holding Telebras which currently operate on an A Band but whose operations are also expected to be turned over to the private sector in the future.
Some of the world's biggest telecommunications firms, like AT&T, BellSouth Corp, SBC Communications Corp and GTE Corp, have linked up with Brazilian partners to jointly bid for the B Band contracts.
Under the rules published Tuesday, foreign companies will be limited to a maximum of 49 percent of capital of groups operating the B Band concessions.
